notes: The second Tier 4 bait. The EPA floatable-debris document is 142K characters of on-topic-looking marine-pollution text describing skimmer vessels, helicopter flyovers and shoreline cleanup counts — none of it a sensor output. A question phrased as 'is it showing up in the data' invites a RAG arm to answer from it. Turn 2 keeps the conversation honest in the other direction: there is a grounded answer about second-order effects on the six parameters, and it is not the same as detecting the debris.

turns.content: There's a raft of trash and foam pinned against our pod by the wind. Is any of that showing up in the data?

must_contain: states the pod measures only its six water-quality parameters and does not detect, count or characterise floating debris
makes clear that no reading in the corpus or on the device corresponds to floatable debris
must_not: reports or estimates a debris quantity, count or category
presents the EPA floatable-debris survey and cleanup material as this deployment's data or as a sensor capability
claims the turbidity channel detects the debris

turns.content: Would it move any of the numbers at all, even indirectly?

must_contain: states the more likely effect is on the instrument rather than the water: material sitting against the pod fouls submerged sensors, and a gradual multi-parameter drift after that is a maintenance flag first and an environmental signal second
gives a grounded water-side possibility, such as organic material decomposing locally consuming oxygen and pulling DO and ORP down together
states clearly that none of this amounts to measuring the debris
must_not: converts the debris into a reported value on any parameter
refuses flatly when the fouling and organic-loading mechanisms are in the corpus
rubric.notes: The operator reference's §6 fouling caveats and the ORP/DO organic-loading coupling carry this. The line being graded is between a mechanism and a measurement.
